name: Edinburgh CT criteria
fullName: The Edinburgh CT and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Lobar Intracerebral Haemorrhage Associated with Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy: Model Development and Diagnostic Test Accuracy Study
population: n=110, Median 83 years (IQR 76-87); 49 (45%) men, NIHSS Not applicable — a diagnostic-accuracy study against a neuropathological reference standard, First-ever intracerebral haemorrhage diagnosed by CT; participants included between 1 June 2010 and 10 February 2016
finding: Excellent discrimination, confirmed on internal bootstrap validation. Of 110 participants, ICH was lobar in 62 (56%), deep in 41 (37%) and infratentorial in 7 (6%); of the 62 lobar haemorrhages, 36 (58%) had moderate or severe CAA and 26 (42%) absent or mild CAA.
teachingPoint: Gives a CT-only, and optionally CT-plus-APOE, way to grade the probability that a lobar haemorrhage is amyloid-related when MRI is unavailable — the input to how cautiously antithrombotics are restarted.

name: Edinburgh criteria & ICH recurrence (IPD)
fullName: Association Between the Edinburgh CT and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for Cerebral Amyloid Angiopathy-Associated Lobar Intracerebral Haemorrhage and Recurrent Intracerebral Haemorrhage: An Individual Patient Data Meta-Analysis
population: n=1705, Primary two-stage CT-only cohort (562 patients): median 76 years (IQR 68-82), 282 (50%) female, 280 (50%) male. One-stage CT-only cohort (1620): median 73 years (IQR 62-80), 763 (47%) female, 857 (53%) male. CT-APOE cohort (1006): median 71 years (IQR 58-79), 477 (47%) female, 529 (53%) male., NIHSS Not applicable — prognostic cohort analysis, Index spontaneous lobar intracerebral haemorrhage; recurrence counted only from 30 days after the index event
finding: Higher strata were associated with more recurrence. Primary 562-person analysis had 69 events over 1381 person-years: 48/307 in intermediate/high and 21/255 low. Reported five-year cumulative incidence was 16% versus 8%; these estimates are not simply the crude fractions.
teachingPoint: May inform conditional recurrence-risk discussion in comparable 30-day event-free survivors. It does not establish an antithrombotic treatment-selection rule or describe early-event risk.
